newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell to close two European blending units.
newsitem.headline: Shell to close two European blending units.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said on Tuesday it would close two blending units in Belgium and the Netherlands as part of a major reorganisation of its European refining operations.
"The blending units at Pernis (Rottterdam) and at Gent in Belgium will be closed by the end of 1998," said Henk Bonder, a Shell Netherlands spokesman.
The closure of the two units comes with the reorganisation and upgrade of two other Shell lubricants plants at Nanterre, near Paris, and at Hamburg.

"A new production centre is being established in Paris, based on the existing Nanterre lubricants blending plants. The centre will be the principle source for the market in lubricants in France, Belgium, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. The centre in Hamburg will also be upgraded," said Bonder.

Earlier, Shell announced it was to sell its 60,000 barrel a day Cressier refinery in Switzerland, continue efforts to improve the profitability of its Shell Haven refinery in England and evaluate its refinery needs in southeast France.
Shell France is participating in an oil industry study, supported by the French government, Bonder said. The study is to be submitted by the end of January 1997.
Shell has one refinery in the southeast of France, the 128,000 barrel per day Berre refinery near Marseille.
